inputs.source: On call engineer's chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request without narrowing allowed targets or requiring confirmation.
The prompt says not to ask for confirmation rather than enforcing any structural approval or destination validation.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
Cloud audit log records production actions
Missing immutable agent action provenance bound to each production action

findings.title: Repudiation: production actions are attributable only to the engineer identity, not separately to deploy-assistant

attack_path.note: Trusted on-call request starts the action
Agent deploys using the engineer's personal access token
Audit record shows only the engineer name

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, and every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript.
Engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Bind each production action to immutable provenance that records the acting agent, the authenticated engineer, the exact requested operation, and a stable request identifier in the system of record rather than only in deletable chat history.
Prevent deletion of chat transcripts that are the sole justification record for production actions, or copy that justification into an immutable audit store before execution.

forecast.watch_signal: Raise if the agent begins taking more production actions per session, if transcript retention is weakened further, or if product changes continue to rely on shared human identity without immutable per-action provenance.

findings.title: Repudiation of irreversible database changes: db migrations can be executed under shared human identity with deletable justification record

attack_path.note: Trusted on-call request reaches irreversible migration capability
Agent runs production migration using the engineer's personal access token
Audit record attributes the action to the engineer rather than separately to the agent
Only justification record is deletable by the engineer

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials and says not to ask for confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Record immutable dual attribution for production migrations so the audit record binds the agent identity, engineer identity, exact migration name, and request context to each execution.
Add a human approval gate or out-of-band confirmation for irreversible production migrations, with raw action review from the system of record.

forecast.watch_signal: Reassess if migration volume rises, if the assistant is allowed to choose migrations from broader context, or if chat retention remains the only justification record for irreversible production changes.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied from the checklist because scripts could not run. Reviewed artifacts were the prompt and runtime notes only; no tool manifest, source code, IaC, or runtime enforcement config was provided. Present risks are driven less by external injection and more by repudiation and attribution gaps: production actions are executed with the engineer's personal token, the cloud audit log records only the engineer identity, and the only request-context record is deletable chat history. The design therefore supports action execution but not strong non-repudiation of whether the engineer or the agent initiated a specific production change.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, IaC, or runtime enforcement configuration was provided, so capability wiring and logging semantics were assessed from documentation only.
No explicit schema field captures non-repudiation strength directly, so repudiation findings were mapped through evidence on audit records, identity attribution, and transcript mutability.
